newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-ANDRETTI TAKES PROVISIONAL POLE IN TORONTO.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ANDRETTI TAKES PROVISIONAL POLE IN TORONTO.

text.p: Michael Andretti's hopes of breaking a 10-race IndyCar winless streak brightened Friday as he captured the provisional pole at the CART Toronto Grand Prix.
Andretti, driving a Swift Ford, had a fastest lap of 59.408 seconds for an average speed of 104.289 mph (167.905 kph).
Andretti has been the most successful driver at the 14-turn, 1.721 mile (2.77 km) circuit with five wins in the last seven races.

He faces a tough challenge from Briton Mark Blundell, a Formula One veteran who won his first CART race in Portland last month. Blundell, driving a Reynard Mercedes Benz, was second fastest, less than half a second off Andretti's pace at 59.894 seconds.
The biggest surprise of the session was a Scotsman with an Italian name, Dario Franchitti, a rookie in this series, who turned in a lap of 60.080 seconds in another Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Brazil's Gil de Ferran, runner-up in Cleveland last week, was fourth fastest at 60.240 seconds in a Reynard Honda.
If Andretti can hold onto the pole after Saturday's final qualifying it would be his 31st, more than any other active driver in the series and it would also end his streak of 39 races without a pole.

Blundell quickly recovered from a scary moment to turn in his good time. "I just clipped the wall in turn six which broke the left rear toe link (a suspension piece). That gave me a fright, because the car jumped completely sideways on me through the fast right-hander," he said.

Going into Sunday's 95-lap race, 11th in the 17-race series, Toronto native Paul Tracy leads fellow-Canadian Greg Moore in the points standings 106 to 95. De Ferran has 94 and Andrettti is fourth with 91.
